USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

distal radius — pattern 4

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 32-year-old mechanic has radial-sided wrist pain after an axial and shearing injury. Imaging demonstrates an isolated fracture separating the radial styloid from the remaining distal radius. The central lunate facet is not depressed, and the carpus is not subluxed. Which distal radius fracture pattern is described?

  1. Chauffeur fracture
  2. Die-punch fracture
  3. Colles fracture
  4. Smith fracture
  5. Barton fracture
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Chauffeur fracture

Chauffeur fracture: An intra-articular fracture of the radial styloid.

Understanding the options

Chauffeur fracture
Chauffeur fracture: An intra-articular fracture of the radial styloid.
Die-punch fracture
Die-punch fracture describes an impacted depression of the distal radial lunate fossa. The case instead matches Chauffeur fracture.
Colles fracture
Colles fracture describes an extra-articular distal radius fracture with dorsal displacement or angulation. The case instead matches Chauffeur fracture.
Smith fracture
Smith fracture describes an extra-articular distal radius fracture with volar displacement or angulation. The case instead matches Chauffeur fracture.
Barton fracture
Barton fracture describes an intra-articular rim shear fracture with associated radiocarpal subluxation or dislocation. The case instead matches Chauffeur fracture.
